newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt impounds Turkish ship until port dues paid.
newsitem.headline: Egypt impounds Turkish ship until port dues paid.

text.p: Egyptian port officials said on Monday they had impounded a Turkish ship after its owners failed to pay about $450,000 for fuel and provisions another of their ships had taken on an earlier trip.

The officials said the Gokceli 1 bulk carrier was impounded after sailing through the Suez Canal. It belongs to the Istanbul-based Akmar Shipping and Trading Company. The firm also owns the bulk carrier Hassan B, which slipped away from Port Said in October without paying its dues.
"The Gokceli will remain impounded until the port, fuel and provisions fees for the Hassan B are paid," an official said.
Egypt has asked Interpol to track down the Hassan B, which had been impounded because it did not pay for services on an earlier trip.
